newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: COURT SUSPENDS FLIGHT RESTRICTIONS AT SCHIPHOL.
newsitem.headline: COURT SUSPENDS FLIGHT RESTRICTIONS AT SCHIPHOL.

text.p: The Haarlem district court has suspended night-flight restrictions at Amsterdam's Schiphol Airport for one week pending a ruling in a case brought against the airport by users, Dutch agency ANP said.
The court ruled that restrictions on night-time take-offs of noisier wide-body aircraft at the airport should be suspended until it gives its verdict next Friday, ANP said.
The night-flight ban, aimed at keeping noise levels within legal limits, is being contested by the Dutch Air Transport Association (ATAN) and several individual airport users.
ATAN has taken Schiphol and the Dutch state to court in a bid to suspend the ban and to allow noise levels to exceed the limits at least until the end of the year.
Other parties to the suit include cargo handler Aero Ground Services and Israeli airline El Al.
El Al said previously it may transfer its freight hub to Liege in Belgium if the ban is upheld.
Aero Ground Services, Schiphol's single biggest independent cargo handler, claims it could lose some 50 percent of its freight volume in the short term with "disastrous consequences" for staff.
